title: EIOPA seeks input on adaptation measures in NatCat insurance under Solvency II
key_claim: EIOPA opened a public consultation on whether adaptation measures should receive dedicated prudential treatment in the Solvency II NatCat standard formula, with responses due by 17 April 2026.
frame_summary: EIOPA argues that insurers should be actively incentivising policyholder adaptation through impact underwriting, and that the prudential rules themselves may be obstructing that by failing to recognise risk-reducing physical measures in capital requirements.
verbatim_quote: The objective of this consultation paper is to assess if a dedicated treatment under Solvency II is justified to better reflect adaptation measures in the NatCat standard formula module beyond the regular calibration of its parameters.
verbatim_list: EIOPA invites stakeholders to provide their feedback on the consultation paper by responding to the questions via the online survey no later than 17th of April 2026.
While progress in the sector can be seen, EIOPA notes that the EU insurance market is still in the early stages of integrating micro-adaptation measures into insurance products.

title: Low Cost, High Yield: The Adaptation and Resilience Investment Opportunity for Infrastructure
key_claim: IFC, AXA Climate and Scientific Climate Ratings argue that adaptation and resilience measures in infrastructure should be treated as a capital-allocation decision rather than an engineering line item, and quantify the exposure at 43 million lost jobs across 49 countries by 2050 without action.
frame_summary: IFC argues that adaptation and resilience spending on infrastructure has been misclassified as an engineering and design cost when it is a financial decision that protects asset value and improves bankability, and that the binding constraints are data, incentives and financing rather than returns.
verbatim_quote: Without action, such climate risks could result in 43 million lost jobs across 49 countries by 2050.
verbatim_list: Natural hazards cost low- and middle-income countries approximately $390 billion annually

The report also identifies gaps in A&R investments and outlines a range of financial mechanisms that can be deployed to mobilize private capital, with actionable recommendations for governments, infrastructure operators, and financiers.

title: Improving insurability, investability and place-based resilience in an era of extreme weather events
key_claim: Constraints on insurability translate into constraints on capital, and assets able to demonstrate resilience are better positioned to attract both investment and favourable insurance terms.
frame_summary: The authors argue that insurability is the leading economic signal of physical climate risk and is becoming a gate on investment flows, and that resilience therefore has to be certified and priced at the level of the place and its shared infrastructure rather than the individual asset.
verbatim_quote: As climate risks intensify, constraints on insurability will increasingly translate into constraints on capital.
verbatim_list: Assets and places that can demonstrate resilience will be better positioned to attract both investment and favourable insurance terms.

An individual facility may be engineered to high resilience standards, but if the storm drainage systems it depends on are inadequate or wildfire risk reduction buffers insufficient, asset-level risk reduction on its own may not be sufficient to meaningfully reduce the risk.
notes: Forum Stories editorial co-authored with Marsh. Cited for the insurability-to-capital mechanism, not as primary data. quote_provenance: manually-verified. title: Face aux risques climatiques, le Gouvernement propose d'adapter le systeme assurantiel francais
key_claim: Claims borne by the French CatNat regime have almost doubled from around EUR 1 billion a year on the 1982-2024 average to nearly EUR 2 billion today, with studies anticipating around EUR 4 billion a year by 2050; the government proposes reviewing the CatNat surcharge rate every five years.
frame_summary: The French Treasury argues that the state-backed CatNat regime is holding for now but that a doubling of claims and a projected further doubling by 2050 require pre-emptive repricing and a shift of burden towards property-level prevention, rather than continued reliance on solidarity-funded compensation alone.
verbatim_quote: La sinistralite prise en charge par le regime Cat Nat a quasiment double, passant d'environ 1 milliard d'euros en moyenne annuelle entre 1982 et 2024 a pres de 2 milliards d'euros aujourd'hui.
verbatim_list: D'ici 2050, plusieurs etudes anticipent une sinistralite moyenne de l'ordre de 4 milliards d'euros par an.
Il examinera tous les cinq ans le taux de surprime Cat Nat afin d'assurer une juste repartition de la charge entre les assures.

title: EIOPA's Financial Stability Report shows continued resilience in insurance amid geopolitical uncertainty and evolving structural risks
key_claim: EIOPA reports that EEA reinsurers continued to benefit from favourable underwriting conditions and strong solvency positions, while telling them to keep monitoring natural-catastrophe exposures.
frame_summary: EIOPA argues that the European insurance sector is currently well capitalised and absorbing shocks, but that supervisors should keep pressure on the longer-run vulnerabilities, including climate-related risks, rather than reading present strength as durable.
verbatim_quote: At the same time, given their exposures, reinsurers should keep monitoring risks associated with natural catastrophes, geopolitical developments and potential disruptions affecting marine and aviation transport.
verbatim_list: Reinsurers in the European Economic Area continued to benefit from favourable underwriting conditions and strong solvency positions.

title: Insurance is vital to combat the effects of climate change
key_claim: A disaster causing damage equivalent to 1% of GDP is estimated to reduce quarterly GDP growth by around 0.24 percentage points with no insurance coverage, 0.15 percentage points at 25% coverage and 0.06 percentage points at 50% coverage.
frame_summary: ECB and EIOPA staff argue that insurance coverage is a materially underweighted macroeconomic shock absorber, and that climate models ignoring the feedback loop between warming, rising premiums and falling coverage systematically understate the economic cost of climate change.
verbatim_quote: For example, a disaster causing damage equivalent to 1% of GDP is estimated to reduce quarterly GDP growth by around 0.24 percentage points if there is no insurance coverage. However, if 25% of the losses are insured, the GDP growth rate is estimated to only decline by around 0.15 percentage points. The effect is even smaller, at around 0.06 percentage points, if half of the losses are insured.
verbatim_list: Yet insurance coverage remains limited, with less than a quarter of catastrophe losses insured in the EU and much lower shares in some countries.
As a result, the macroeconomic costs of climate change may be significantly underestimated by models that do not account for declining insurance coverage.
notes: Policy summary of Giuzio et al., European Economic Review Vol 182, 105210. Authors affiliated to the ECB and EIOPA; brief carries the standard non-attribution disclaimer. quote_provenance: manually-verified. title: Appetite for reinsurance brings moment for creativity. NA cat rates 20-25%+ down: Gallagher Re
key_claim: At the 1 July 2026 renewals, North American property catastrophe rates fell 20% to 25% or more for the best performing accounts, with Gallagher Re's global CEO describing the market as mid-cycle rather than at the bottom.
frame_summary: Artemis reports Gallagher Re arguing that record reinsurance capital and flat demand have produced a buyer's market in which the durable prize is structural improvement to programmes rather than the price cut itself, and warns that risk-adjusted rate adequacy may be leaking through more creative structures.
verbatim_quote: Demand for reinsurance opportunities outstripped demand for protection at the July renewals, resulting in softening prices and North American property catastrophe rates tumbling 20% to 25% or more in some cases.
verbatim_list: We are mid-cycle, not at the bottom

Cedants are increasingly implementing tailored solutions to manage earnings volatility and optimize capital efficiency, using improved market conditions to enhance structure alongside achieving rate reductions,

title: Aon Report Finds Below-Average Global Catastrophe Losses Masked Significant Regional Impacts in H1 2026
date_evidence: DUBLIN, July 22, 2026 - Aon plc (NYSE: AON), a leading global professional services firm, today published its Global Catastrophe Recap: First Half of 2026 report
key_claim: Global economic losses in the first half of 2026 totalled $111 billion, 25 percent below the 21st-century average and the lowest first-half total since 2018, while US catastrophes generated approximately $36 billion in insured losses, 75 percent of the global total.
frame_summary: Aon argues that headline aggregate loss totals are a misleading risk indicator, because a below-average total concealed an above-average count of billion-dollar insured events and extreme regional concentration, so historical loss experience is becoming an unreliable guide for risk decisions.
verbatim_quote: Global economic losses totaled $111 billion during H1 of 2026, 25 percent below the 21st-century average and the lowest first half total since 2018.
verbatim_list: Overall, U.S. natural catastrophes generated approximately $36 billion in insured losses, representing 75 percent of global insured losses in H1 2026.
